facts.fact: There are exactly three DR scripts plus one shared library: scripts/backup.sh (214 lines), scripts/restore.sh (198), scripts/dr-drill.sh (398), scripts/_lib/pg-restore-filter.sh (119). No other backup tooling exists in the repo.

backup.sh produces exactly four artefacts in $BACKUP_ROOT/$(date +%Y%m%d)/: postgres.sql.gz (pg_dumpall --clean --if-exists of the WHOLE cluster, gzip -9), storage.tar.gz (tar of the uploads tree), caddy-logs.tar.gz (best-effort), manifest.txt (host, completed_at, image_tag, file list).

The Postgres artefact is a cluster-wide pg_dumpall SQL script, not per-database custom dumps. It therefore includes libriant_control, every tenant_* database, AND all cluster globals — roles with their SCRAM password hashes. Restoring is `psql -f`, never pg_restore.

backup.sh runs pg_dumpall INSIDE the postgres container via `docker compose exec -T postgres`, so no psql/pg_dumpall is needed on the host and client/server major-version skew cannot occur for the nightly.

backup.sh has five hard ABORT gates before it will call a run successful: (1) the control-DB tenant-host query failing; (2) any tenant whose dbUrl host is not postgres/pgbouncer/localhost/127.0.0.1 (off-host tenant, unless BACKUP_ALLOW_OFFHOST_TENANTS=1); (3) a postgres.sql.gz smaller than 1024 bytes; (4) `gzip -t` failing on postgres.sql.gz or storage.tar.gz; (5) a missing STORAGE_DIR (unless BACKUP_ALLOW_NO_STORAGE=1).

The off-host-tenant guard queries the Prisma camelCase quoted column "dbUrl"; an unquoted db_url would fold to lowercase and abort EVERY backup. This is called out in the script itself as a prior failure mode.

backup.sh resolves the uploads path on the host by `docker volume inspect ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_storage --format '{{.Mountpoint}}'`, falling back to /var/lib/docker/volumes/<project>_storage/_data and then /srv/libriant/storage. It does NOT use LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT.
`storage` is a NAMED docker volume, mounted into api and worker at the in-container path /srv/libriant/storage. /srv/libriant/storage does not exist on the host as a data directory.

The deployed stack chains a second compose file, docker-compose.volume.yml, which rebinds pg_data, redis_data, storage and caddy_data to ${LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT:-/mnt/libriant}/{postgres,redis,storage,caddy} via driver_opts type=none/o=bind. caddy_logs and caddy_config are NOT rebound and stay plain docker volumes.

Neither backup.sh nor restore.sh includes the volume overlay in its default COMPOSE_FILE — both default to docker-compose.prod.yml alone. backup.sh documents this as harmless for `exec`; restore.sh also uses that same file for `dc up -d api worker web`.

CADDY_LOG_DIR defaults to /var/lib/docker/volumes/${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_caddy_logs/_data, which is correct: caddy_logs is one of the two volumes the overlay does not rebind, and Caddy writes /var/log/caddy/access.log into it.

WHAT IS NOT BACKED UP, established by reading backup.sh end to end: /srv/libriant/.env.prod (deliberate); the Cloudflare origin cert + key at $DATA_ROOT/caddy/origin/ (caddy_data is not touched); caddy_config; Redis (redis_data, appendonly yes) — which holds the BullMQ queues, rate-limit counters and idempotency keys; docker images (they come from GHCR); the built marketing site. backup.sh has no code path that reads any of these.

facts.fact: There is NO WAL archiving and NO point-in-time recovery. The postgres service command sets only shared_preload_libraries and max_connections; no archive_mode, no archive_command, no pgBackRest/wal-g anywhere in the repo. RPO is therefore the cron interval: up to ~24 hours of loss.

Local retention is BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS (default 14), pruned at the START of each run with `find $BACKUP_ROOT -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -mtime +$BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS -exec rm -rf`. BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS=14 is the only backup value ensure-env.sh writes.

Off-site is a single line: `rclone copy --quiet "$dest" "$RCLONE_REMOTE/$day"` into a per-day path. It is `copy`, not `sync`; there is no --delete, no `rclone delete --min-age`, no lifecycle rule, and no prune of the remote anywhere in the repo. Off-site dailies accumulate forever.

facts.fact: THE RESTORE PROCEDURE AS IT NOW WORKS, step by step from scripts/restore.sh: (0) resolve the day dir, require postgres.sql.gz, require --yes; (1) `gunzip -t` both archives BEFORE touching anything; (2) pre-flight the stream filter and die unless it matches exactly 2 self-role statements; (3) `dc stop api worker web pgbouncer`; (4) pg_terminate_backend every session except template0 and self; (5) install `trap restart_apps EXIT`; (6) pipe `pg_restore_preamble $PG_ROLE` followed by the filtered dump into `dc exec -T postgres psql -U $PG_ROLE -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`; (7) move any existing $STORAGE_DIR contents into $STORAGE_DIR/.pre-restore.<ts>/ then untar storage.tar.gz into the now-clean tree; (8) print cells,plans counts, check each tenant_* DB has 4/4 extensions, and DIE if the control plane lists more tenants than there are tenant databases.
restore.sh restores only Postgres and storage. caddy-logs.tar.gz is written by backup.sh but never read by restore.sh, and .env.prod / the origin cert are neither backed up nor restored.

facts.fact: THE 2026-08-22 FIX, verified by running it locally: pg_restore_filter_count returns exactly 2 for a synthetic pg_dumpall prologue; pg_restore_filter removes only `DROP ROLE IF EXISTS libriant;` and `CREATE ROLE libriant;`, keeps the `ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD`, leaves other roles alone, stops dead at the first `\connect` (a `CREATE ROLE libriant;` line after \connect survives untouched); pg_restore_preamble emits the template1 datistemplate=false UPDATE plus `ALTER ROLE "libriant" RESET ALL;` and `ALTER ROLE "libriant" WITH CONNECTION LIMIT -1 VALID UNTIL 'infinity';`.
facts.source: RAN: bash -c '. scripts/_lib/pg-restore-filter.sh; pg_restore_filter_count/pg_restore_filter/pg_restore_preamble against a synthetic prologue' → count=2, filtered output and preamble exactly as described

facts.fact: The bug the fix addresses: a pg_dumpall --clean script DROPs and CREATEs the very role psql connects as; under ON_ERROR_STOP=1 psql stops there — AFTER the DROP DATABASE wave. Reproduced at the time as psql exit 3 with zero databases left.

The filter is deliberately prologue-scoped and count-asserted because both failure modes were hit: an unanchored match would delete `CREATE ROLE libriant;` from inside COPY data or a dollar-quoted function body while psql still exits 0, and a silently non-matching pattern would let the restore wipe the cluster exactly as before.
facts.source: scripts/_lib/pg-restore-filter.sh:19-32; scripts/dr-drill.sh:162-169 (the dr_canary function fixture that proves the scope)

facts.fact: The template1 hazard is real and now handled unconditionally: pg_dumpall emits a bare `DROP DATABASE template1;` and only precedes it with the datistemplate=false UPDATE when the SOURCE's template1 was still a template — which it stops being the first time a cluster is restored into. So a second-generation dump kills a pristine target with 'cannot drop a template database', after the DROP wave. That is exactly the rebuilt-host path.

A pg_dumpall restore onto a REBUILT host overwrites the target's superuser password with the SOURCE's hash. After a cross-host restore, POSTGRES_PASSWORD in the freshly minted .env.prod is wrong and the stack cannot authenticate; the correct value is the password-manager entry for the SOURCE host. This is asserted, not assumed, by the drill.
facts.source: scripts/dr-drill.sh:295-385 (chk "target's stored verifier is now the SOURCE's", "target REJECTS its own former password"); docs/server-handbook.md:500-511

facts.fact: ALTER ROLE only OVERLAYS — pg_dumpall omits CONNECTION LIMIT when -1 and VALID UNTIL when null, so drift on the target survives a 'successful' restore (measured: target kept CONNECTION LIMIT 7 and statement_timeout=1s). That is why pg_restore_preamble resets them first; an expired VALID UNTIL would otherwise present as 'password authentication failed' long after anyone is looking.

WHAT THE DRILL COVERS (30 checks, per the audit's execution): a negative control that password auth is actually enforced; pg_dumpall with backup.sh's exact flags; deliberate drift of the restoring role; a partial disaster (two live DBs corrupted, a third dropped, a role dropped) rather than a clean wipe; the filter pre-flight count; psql exit code; a locale-independent SQLSTATE error count (compose sets LANG=el_GR.UTF-8 so grepping for 'ERROR' would fail); full row census per table from the catalogue; exact extension set with version+schema; every sequence's last_value; byte-identical pg_dump --schema-only diffs; the database set with encoding and collation; grants; other roles; the restoring role's attributes, password hash and live TCP authentication; and with --cross-cluster, the rebuilt-host password flip.

facts.fact: WHAT THE DRILL DOES NOT COVER: (a) storage — no tarball leg at all, so backup.sh's tar and restore.sh's untar are never exercised; (b) backup.sh itself — the drill re-implements only `pg_dumpall --clean --if-exists | gzip -9` inline at line 210, so the off-host-tenant guard, the volume-mountpoint resolution, the size/gzip gates, the prune, the manifest and the rclone push are all untested; (c) restore.sh itself — it sources _lib/pg-restore-filter.sh but never invokes restore.sh, so the container stop/start ordering, the `trap restart_apps EXIT`, the archive validation and the tenant-count assertion are untested; (d) the off-site leg — nothing ever pulls a backup back from RCLONE_REMOTE; (e) scale/RTO — the fixture is 502 rows and a ~5 KB dump; (f) restoring an OLD dump against NEWER code (Prisma migration drift).

facts.fact: The drill runs in CI on every push, twice: `pnpm dr:drill` against a dedicated postgres-drill service on port 5433 (NOT the shared 5432, because pg_dumpall is cluster-wide and the drill destroys everything it dumped), and `pnpm dr:drill --cross-cluster` against a second cluster on 5434 running POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust. AUDIT BLOCKER privacy-legal-02 — TRUE CURRENT POSITION: backups are plaintext everywhere (host and off-site), and the off-site copy is never pruned, while locales/en/legal/dpa.md:85 contractually promises 'regular encrypted backups with restore testing' (el: dpa.md:100) and locales/en/legal/privacy.md:77-78 states backups are 'rotated on a rolling [14]-day cycle, after which deleted copies age out of backups' (el: privacy.md:89-90). Local dailies genuinely do age out at BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS; off-site ones never do, so an Art. 17 erasure never propagates out of the off-site copy. Both statements are untrue as deployed. It is one of the 9 blockers marked blocks:'public-launch'.

The exposure that makes privacy-legal-02 a blocker is specifically the off-site leg, not the host: a plaintext pg_dumpall of every library's member registry (fullName, dateOfBirth, address, phone, email, staffNotes, and the named loan/reservation/fine history including school-library children) sitting on a Hetzner Storage Box, retained forever, reachable with the rclone credentials that live on the same host. The auditor explicitly notes that encrypting on the app host is of limited value against an attacker who already has that host.

Compounding blocker: the Caddy access log is tarred into the same unencrypted backup, and password-reset / email-verification URLs carry their raw token in the query string through a Caddyfile whose global `log { format json }` block has no URI filter. So the backup contains live account-takeover tokens in cleartext.

OPEN HIGH (reliability-05, not in BLOCKERS.json but unfixed): restore.sh:30 defaults STORAGE_DIR to /srv/libriant/storage — the IN-CONTAINER path. backup.sh got the docker-volume-inspect resolution and a hard abort on a missing dir; restore.sh got neither. A default-invocation restore does `mkdir -p` on a fresh host directory no container mounts, untars into it, logs 'storage restored' and exits 0, having recovered zero files. The tenant-count sanity check only counts databases, so it stays green.
OPEN HIGH (reliability-09): a backup that never runs, or aborts every night, is undetectable — no cron installer, no failure ping (heartbeat is success-only and unset), and no alert delivery at all.

INTERACTION HAZARD the audit does not connect: restore.sh's EXIT trap runs `dc up -d api worker web`, and api depends_on migrate with condition service_completed_successfully. Blocker supply-chain-06 establishes that the migrate one-shot currently exits 1 because the images pin corepack to pnpm@9.15.4 while package.json declares packageManager pnpm@11.22.0. So as the tree stands today, a restore would complete the database work and then fail to bring the application back up.

facts.fact: THE HEADLINE: the stack BUILDS but does NOT RUN today. Precise operator experience on a correctly-prepared box: preflight passes, `dc build` succeeds (10-20 min), `caddy validate` passes, then `dc up -d` fails because the one-shot `migrate` service exits 1. deploy-on-host.sh catches it, dumps the last 200 lines of migrate logs and `dc ps`, and dies with 'compose up failed.' api/web/worker never start. Nothing is left half-applied in the database — migrate exits before touching it.

Root cause of the migrate failure (blocker supply-chain-06): package.json declares `"packageManager": "pnpm@11.22.0"` while all three Dockerfiles run `corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate`. Corepack always honours the nearest package.json `packageManager` and ignores `prepare --activate` (which only sets a fallback for projects declaring nothing). The pin is inert.

Why it is fatal and not self-healing in the API image: the runtime stage is `FROM base AS runtime`, NOT from `deps`. The only pnpm ever written into COREPACK_HOME=/opt/corepack in the shipped image is 9.15.4 (line 30); the `pnpm install` that caches 11.22.0 happens in the `deps` layer (line 54), which runtime never inherits. Line 31 `chmod -R a+rX` grants read+traverse but NOT write, and the dir is root-owned; line 97 sets `USER node`. So the node user cannot write the cache. Audit reproduced the exact stderr: `Failed to create cache directory. Please ensure the user has write access to the target directory (<COREPACK_HOME>/v1)`, EXIT=1.

ADDITIONAL fact the audit did not state, and which rules out the obvious workaround: the `migrate` service is attached to `networks: [data]` only, and the `data` network is `internal: true`. So even if /opt/corepack were made writable (e.g. by restoring `user: root`), migrate has NO route to registry.npmjs.org and still cannot fetch pnpm 11.22.0. The only fix is to bake the correct version into the image and rebuild — a host-side compose edit cannot work, and `git reset --hard` in deploy-on-host.sh:83 would discard it anyway.

The error message the operator actually reads is misleading. prod-bootstrap.sh turns the corepack exit into `[bootstrap] FATAL: control-plane migration failed. If this is a P3009 'failed migration' or drift, inspect with 'prisma migrate status' and resolve with 'prisma migrate resolve' before redeploying.` The real corepack line appears above it in the same dumped log. A runbook must say: ignore the P3009 advice, scroll up for the corepack line.

Second corepack defect, independent of migrate: apps/web/Dockerfile sets NO COREPACK_HOME (line 9 is a bare `corepack prepare` as root), line 64 is `USER node`, line 68 is `CMD ["pnpm", "--filter", "@libriant/web", "start"]`. The web container's PID 1 IS corepack; it finds an empty /home/node/.cache/node/corepack and downloads pnpm 11.22.0 from npmjs.org at EVERY container start before Next.js boots. web is on the `app` bridge network so it succeeds — meaning every web restart depends on npmjs.org and on host egress.

Nothing in CI catches either defect: no workflow builds or runs these images except deploy.yml itself (which is workflow_dispatch-only). `grep 'docker build|docker compose|Dockerfile' .github/workflows/*.yml` hits only deploy.yml lines 103/115/130 (buildx push) and 295-333 (the remote ssh block). verify.yml and ci.yml contain none.

The exact fix and its cost: change three lines to `corepack prepare pnpm@11.22.0 --activate` (apps/api/Dockerfile:30, apps/web/Dockerfile:9, infra/caddy/Dockerfile:16), add `ENV COREPACK_HOME=/opt/corepack` + `chmod -R a+rX` to the web image, add the `+sha224.<hash>` integrity suffix to package.json:6. Because package.json is baked (only scripts/ and locales/ are bind-mounted into migrate), this requires a full rebuild — it cannot be hot-patched on the box.

PREREQUISITE 1 — packages. deploy-on-host.sh enforces only `command -v docker`. Everything else is unenforced: git (needed at line 45/80/83/86), openssl (ensure-env.sh:61 uses `openssl rand`), curl (health gate line 172/178). Absence of git or openssl fails mid-run with a raw 'command not found', not a named precondition.

PREREQUISITE 1b — `command -v docker` does NOT prove the invoking user can reach the daemon. If `deploy` is not in the `docker` group (or has not re-logged in since being added), preflight passes; the two prune calls at lines 122-123 are `|| true` and SILENTLY swallow the permission error; the failure only surfaces at `dc build` as 'permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket'.

PREREQUISITE 2 — the `deploy` user. Created by `adduser --disabled-password --gecos "" deploy` + `usermod -aG docker deploy` + copying root's authorized_keys. Nothing in any script creates or checks this user; the whole runbook simply assumes you are `deploy`.

PREREQUISITE 3 — directories and ownership, in this order. (a) `/srv/libriant` owned by deploy (holds the checkout and .env.prod). (b) `/var/log/libriant` owned by deploy (only used by the backup cron). (c) `/mnt/libriant` must exist — deploy-on-host.sh:48 enforces existence, but NOT that it is a separate mount. (d) `/mnt/libriant/{postgres,redis,storage,caddy}` — all four enforced by deploy-on-host.sh:55-57 with a named error. (e) `/mnt/libriant/backups` — NOT enforced anywhere; nothing in the deploy path touches backups.

PREREQUISITE 3f — `sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/libriant/storage` is REQUIRED and enforced by NOTHING. api/worker run as USER node (uid 1000) and the bind mount keeps the host's ownership; Docker will not chown a bind mount. Skipping it gives a fully healthy stack that throws EACCES on the first cover upload, because /readyz checks Postgres and Redis and never touches storage. Postgres and Redis do NOT need this — their official images start as root and chown their data dir via su-exec.

PREREQUISITE 4 — the git checkout at /srv/libriant/app. deploy-on-host.sh:45 enforces `[ -d $APP_DIR/.git ]`. It then runs `git fetch --quiet origin` and `git reset --hard origin/main` on EVERY deploy, so the remote MUST be named `origin` and MUST be fetchable non-interactively by the deploy user. The repo is documented as PRIVATE, so this needs a credential — the working path is the read-only GitHub Deploy Key + ~/.ssh/config from deployment-hetzner.md:372-375 and an SSH clone. A missing credential fails at line 80 under `set -e` with a git auth error, not a named precondition.

PREREQUISITE 5 — /srv/libriant/.env.prod. deploy-on-host.sh:47 enforces the file exists and names the fix command. The file must be created by ONE interactive run of `bash scripts/ensure-env.sh /srv/libriant/.env.prod` (no --auto), because --auto never prompts. ensure-env.sh itself does `umask 077`, mkdir -p, touch, chmod 600 — permissions are enforced.

ensure-env.sh generates and never overwrites: SESSION_SECRET, HASH_PEPPER, ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET, MFA_MASTER_KEY (all hex-32) and POSTGRES_PASSWORD (hex-24). Every one of these is a hard `${VAR:?}` requirement in the compose file, so the fail-fast is real but is always pre-empted by --auto on every deploy.

Only TWO values a human must supply, and they are the difference between a green deploy and one you cannot log into: ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL and ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD. deploy-on-host.sh warns (yellow, non-fatal) if the EMAIL is empty. It does NOT check the PASSWORD. prod-bootstrap.sh requires BOTH to be non-empty. So email-set + password-blank = a completely silent skip with no warning at all.

IMAGE_OWNER is NOT actually required for an on-host deploy. `ask` skips it under --auto and the template sync explicitly skips the key, so it stays absent; compose then falls back to `${IMAGE_OWNER:-libriant}` and `dc build` tags the images locally as ghcr.io/libriant/libriant-{api,web,caddy}:<sha>. IMAGE_OWNER only matters if you ever pull. deployment-hetzner.md:409 presenting it as mandatory is misleading for the manual path.

ensure-env.sh's LAST step copies any key present in .env.prod.example but absent from .env.prod, verbatim. That is how MAINTENANCE_HARD, RCLONE_REMOTE, DESKTOP_RELEASE_REPO/TOKEN, SMTP_URL, EMAIL_FROM etc. arrive. It runs after the generators so secrets keep their generated values, and it skips IMAGE_OWNER because the template ships the placeholder `your-github-owner`.

PREREQUISITE 6 — the Cloudflare origin certificate at /mnt/libriant/caddy/origin/{origin.crt,origin.key}. deploy-on-host.sh:64-68 enforces BOTH files with a named error, because every HTTPS vhost imports the `cloudflare_origin` snippet (`tls /etc/caddy/origin/origin.crt ...`) and `caddy validate` provisions file certificates — a missing cert reports 'Caddyfile is invalid' when the Caddyfile is fine. The compose bind mount would otherwise auto-create an EMPTY directory, hiding the cause. The PEMs are only in the password manager; no backup contains them.

LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT set in .env.prod is IGNORED by deploy-on-host.sh. DATA_ROOT is resolved at line 25 from the shell env (default /mnt/libriant), the preflight checks run against it, and after sourcing .env.prod line 105 re-exports LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT" — overwriting whatever the file said. Changing it in .env.prod silently does nothing. To relocate data you must export LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT in the shell before invoking the script.

IMAGE_TAG ordering is deliberate and load-bearing: .env.prod ships IMAGE_TAG=latest and `set -a; . $ENV_FILE` would clobber the computed SHA, so `export IMAGE_TAG="$TAG"` comes AFTER the source. The tag is the 12-char short SHA with `-dirty` appended when the tree differs.

Deploy order once preconditions hold: prune (72h, best-effort) → `dc build` → `caddy validate` in a throwaway container BEFORE anything is recreated → `dc up -d --remove-orphans --force-recreate` → `caddy reload` (fallback: recreate caddy) → 180s health loop. The health gate is intentionally local-only: http://localhost/healthz, plus https://libriant.com/ via `--resolve libriant.com:443:127.0.0.1` (NOT `-H 'Host:'`, which offers SNI `localhost` that the origin cert does not cover), plus container health for api/web/worker.

Bring-up order inside compose: postgres (healthy) → migrate (runs to completion) → api → web; worker gates on migrate+postgres+redis; caddy gates only on api/web `service_started` (deliberately loosened so an app outage does not take the marketing site down). `dc build` does not build `migrate` (no build section) — it reuses the api image, which is why the api build must be part of the same run.

`--skip-build` is unsafe on a first deploy: with no locally built images compose falls back to pulling ghcr.io/libriant/libriant-*:<sha>, which does not exist. Use `--dry-run` first (runs every precondition check and prints commit + tag without touching anything), then a full build.

Build resource facts stated in the repo: `next build` peaks ~1.8 GB with no heap cap and scales workers by core count; exit 137 = OOM; documented mitigation is swap or building one service at a time. Budget 10-20 min and ~15-20 GB of /var/lib/docker for a cold first build. NOTE: these numbers were written for the DEAD box's hardware and are unvalidated on 195.201.13.95.

A green first deploy has ZERO backups and says nothing about it. The nightly job is installed only by a hand-run `sudo tee /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup`; deploy-on-host.sh never checks for it. Offsite requires RCLONE_REMOTE, which ensure-env.sh does not default and the template ships empty; backup.sh then only logs 'WARN: RCLONE_REMOTE unset — NO OFF-SITE COPY' to a file nobody reads.

Do NOT trust `web=healthy` in the deploy gate as evidence the app works. The web healthcheck hits /api/healthz, which returns a constant {status:'ok'} and touches no dependency. A wrong API_INTERNAL_URL or a broken `app` network is invisible: all four gate signals go green and every page renders an error. (`api=healthy` IS meaningful — it probes /readyz.)

prod-bootstrap.sh step 4 (tenant migrations) and step 5 (first admin) are BEST-EFFORT — they `|| echo ... (non-fatal)` and migrate still exits 0. Only control-plane migrate (line 35) and seed (line 41) are fatal. On a first deploy step 4 is a no-op (no tenants yet), but step 5 failing means a green deploy nobody can log into, with no warning from deploy-on-host.sh.

`migrate` doubles as the operator shell: it carries the repo scripts/ + locales/ bind mounts and the full DB env, so `dc run --rm --no-deps migrate sh -lc 'cd /app && pnpm <task>'` is the escape hatch for re-seed, tenant:create, etc. Because scripts/ is bind-mounted from the host checkout, a change to prod-bootstrap.sh takes effect without a rebuild — but a change to package.json or a Dockerfile does not.

Toolchain actually pinned in the repo on 2026-08-23: node:26-alpine (api, web, caddy build stage), postgres:16-alpine, redis:8-alpine, edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0, caddy:2-alpine (final stage of the custom edge image), pnpm 11.22.0, engines.node >=26. The Caddy image is CUSTOM — it bakes the rendered marketing site into /srv/libriant/site — so `caddy:2-alpine` is a base, never the running image.

The `caddy` image build runs `pnpm --filter @libriant/site build` in STRICT mode, which refuses to emit while apps/site/site.config.json holds a [PLACEHOLDER]. I checked: site.config.json currently contains no [PLACEHOLDER], so the build passes today. But privacy-legal-01 requires setting identity.controllerName once the entity is registered — if that ever reverts to a placeholder, the CADDY image build fails, not just the legal page.

Edge /readyz and /metrics are NOT real probes. The `maintenance_check` snippet unconditionally answers `respond "ok" 200` for /healthz, /readyz and /metrics on every vhost that imports it — including the app vhost. So an external `curl https://<host>/readyz` can never reflect API health, and piping it to jq will fail on the literal string 'ok'.

9 of the 12 blockers block public launch. The three that do not are performance-01 (blocks scale) and billing-03/billing-04 (block first-paying-customer). A first deploy is therefore legitimate as a PRIVATE, not-in-DNS box — deploy-on-host.sh even prints 'This box is not in DNS yet, so nothing is public' on success — but the runbook must not route an operator from first deploy into the cutover.

facts.fact: The `dc` helper is a shell FUNCTION added to deploy's ~/.bashrc, not a script in the repo. Definition: `dc() { ( cd /srv/libriant/app && docker compose -f infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml -f infra/compose/docker-compose.volume.yml "$@" ); }`, preceded by `export COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=libriant`, `export LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT=/mnt/libriant`, and a `set -a; . /srv/libriant/.env.prod; set +a` sourcing line.

Two overlaid compose files is correct: deploy-on-host.sh uses `FILES="-f infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml -f infra/compose/docker-compose.volume.yml"` and defines its own private `dc()` around it.

The volume overlay rebinds ONLY four named volumes to host paths under $LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT: pg_data->/postgres, redis_data->/redis, storage->/storage, caddy_data->/caddy. caddy_config and caddy_logs are NOT overridden, so they stay on the boot disk under /var/lib/docker/volumes/.
Caddy's access log is configured `roll_size 100mb` / `roll_keep 14` = up to ~1.4 GB, and it lands in the caddy_logs named volume, i.e. on the ROOT filesystem, not on /mnt/libriant.
Container stdout logs are capped by a shared anchor: json-file driver, max-size 50m, max-file 5, applied to every service. That is up to 250 MB per service on the boot disk.

The only host log file the project writes is /var/log/libriant/backup.log (and optionally /var/log/libriant/fleet.log), created by the cron redirect. Nothing anywhere installs logrotate for it — `find . -name 'logrotate*'` returns nothing.

The nightly backup cron is `15 2 * * *` (02:15) run as user `deploy`, installed by a hand-typed `sudo tee /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup`. No script, workflow, or deploy step installs it; deploy-on-host.sh never checks it exists.

backup.sh defaults BACKUP_ROOT to /srv/libriant/backups (the ROOT volume). ensure-env.sh writes only `LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT=/mnt/libriant` and never writes BACKUP_ROOT, STORAGE_DIR, RCLONE_REMOTE or BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL, so every invocation must pass BACKUP_ROOT explicitly or backups fill /.

facts.fact: backup.sh auto-resolves the uploads path via `docker volume inspect ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_storage` and HARD ABORTS if the directory is missing. restore.sh does NOT: it defaults STORAGE_DIR to the in-container path /srv/libriant/storage, mkdir -p's it, untars into it and logs 'storage restored' with no existence or file-count check.

backup.sh ABORTS the entire nightly run (exit 1) if any tenant's control-plane `dbUrl` host is not one of postgres/pgbouncer/localhost/127.0.0.1, unless BACKUP_ALLOW_OFFHOST_TENANTS=1. Relocating one tenant off-box therefore silently stops ALL backups.

backup.sh has six distinct abort paths (control-DB query failure, off-host tenant, <1 KiB dump, either gzip integrity check, missing storage dir). The only notification channel is BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL, which fires on SUCCESS ONLY at the very end, after rclone, and is absent from .env.prod.example.

restore.sh has a pre-flight stream filter that counts self-role statements and refuses to run unless exactly 2 match, having touched nothing. It also gzip-tests every archive before any DROP, stops api/worker/web AND pgbouncer, and terminates every other backend on every non-template0 database.

`pnpm dr:drill` really does run on every push to main and every PR: ci.yml triggers on push/PR and calls the reusable verify.yml, which runs the drill on port 5433 (a throwaway cluster) plus `--cross-cluster` against a second cluster on 5434.

The operator shell on the box is `dc run --rm --no-deps migrate sh -lc 'cd /app && pnpm <task>'`. The `migrate` service is the ONLY service that bind-mounts the repo scripts/ directory (`../../scripts:/app/scripts:ro`); api, web and worker do not.

Adding a tenant by hand is `dc run --rm --no-deps migrate sh -lc "cd /app && pnpm tenant:create -- --slug=… --name=… --owner-email=… --owner-name=… --plan=… --billing-mode=…"`. tenant-create.ts requires --slug, --name, --owner-email, --owner-name; supports --primary-email, --default-locale, --plan, --billing-mode, --paid-until, --cell, --owner-password, --dry-run; is idempotent on slug and tears the physical DB down on late failure.
The `migrate` service is attached to the `data` network ONLY, and `data` is declared `internal: true` — containers on it have no route to the host or the internet.

Migrations run as the one-shot `migrate` service via `sh /app/scripts/prod-bootstrap.sh`, gated by `depends_on: condition: service_completed_successfully` on api and worker. Within it only control-plane `db:migrate:deploy` and `db:seed` are FATAL; `ingest:help`, `tenant:migrate` and `admin:bootstrap` are best-effort and the one-shot still exits 0.

Tenant-schema fan-out is `pnpm tenant:migrate` (scripts/tenant-migrate.ts) with --only=slug,slug, --include-archived, --dry-run, --concurrency=N (default 1, capped 16). Individual tenant failures do not stop the batch; it exits non-zero at the end.

tenant-relocate.ts opens a per-tenant `read_only` system-mode window, waits --drain-seconds (must exceed the 30s system-mode cache TTL), pg_dump/pg_restore, migrates, verifies, rewrites tenants.db_url + cell_id, busts the Redis key `tenant:slug:<slug>`, then ends the window. Maintenance mode has TWO independent layers. (1) Application: SystemModeKind = normal(0) / under_construction(1) / read_only(2) / out_of_order(3) / maintenance(3), driven by owner-only admin endpoints POST /admin/system-mode/global, POST /admin/system-mode/tenants/:tenantId, POST /admin/system-mode/events/:id/end, DELETE /admin/system-mode/events/:id, plus GET current|scheduled|history. (2) Edge: `MAINTENANCE_HARD=true` on the caddy service serves the static maintenance.html.
The marketing-site vhost deliberately imports maintenance_check but NOT maintenance_takeover, so libriant.com stays readable while the app is in hard maintenance.

/healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /system-mode/*, /admin/system-mode/*, /admin/auth/*, /webhooks/stripe and /apply are in ALWAYS_PASS so a maintenance window can always be lifted; /admin/* and /auth/admin/* are gated by allowAdminBypass; active impersonation sessions also pass.

Every service except `migrate` carries `restart: unless-stopped` (migrate is `restart: 'no'`). Docker's unless-stopped policy does not restart a container that was manually stopped — so `dc stop` followed by a reboot leaves the whole stack DOWN until someone runs `dc up -d`.
Grafana is published on 127.0.0.1:3300 (host) -> 3000 (container). The correct tunnel is `ssh -L 3300:localhost:3300 deploy@195.201.13.95`.

The ten shipped alert rules are TargetDown, LibriantApiDown, HostLowMemory, HostSwapping, HostDiskFilling, HostDiskCritical, HostHighCPU, LibriantPgConnectionsHigh, LibriantPgConnectionsCritical, LibriantPgCacheHitLow. Detection time for any outage is 'until the operator next looks'.

The security model as CODE stands at: 80 and 443 published by the caddy container (which bypasses ufw via iptables), data network internal:true, and NO Cloudflare-range restriction anywhere. The Caddyfile unconditionally does `header_up X-Real-IP {http.request.header.CF-Connecting-IP}` on all three vhosts. The host toolchain installed by the runbook is `git curl ufw fail2ban unattended-upgrades ca-certificates` plus Docker — no Node, no pnpm. deploy-on-host.sh preconditions: $APP_DIR/.git exists, $ENV_FILE exists, $DATA_ROOT exists, docker present, $DATA_ROOT/{postgres,redis,storage,caddy} all exist (note: `backups` is in the mkdir hint but NOT checked), and $DATA_ROOT/caddy/origin/{origin.crt,origin.key} both present. deploy-on-host.sh prunes images/build cache older than 72h before every build, validates the Caddyfile with `caddy validate` before recreating anything, uses `up -d --remove-orphans --force-recreate`, reloads Caddy, then polls up to 180s for edge 200 + site 200 + api/web/worker container health. Nothing is rolled back on failure.

`git reset --hard "$REF"` is real in the MANUAL path too — deploy-on-host.sh does it deliberately to mirror CI. Host-local edits to tracked files are destroyed on every deploy unless --no-fetch is passed.

Image tags are the 12-char short SHA with a `-dirty` suffix when the working tree is unclean; IMAGE_TAG is exported AFTER sourcing .env.prod precisely so the file's default `latest` cannot silently override it.

Postgres is postgres:16-alpine with `max_connections=200`, mem_limit 2g, cpus 2. pgbouncer is edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0, POOL_MODE=transaction, MAX_CLIENT_CONN=500, DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE=20, and is configured for a SINGLE database (DB_NAME: libriant_control) — tenant databases do not go through it. Redis is redis:8-alpine with appendonly yes and `--maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` but NO `--maxmemory`, which makes the policy inert.

Per-container caps already exist in the compose file and are the real capacity ceiling to reason about: caddy 256m/1cpu, api 1g/1.5cpu, web 768m/1cpu, worker 1g/1cpu, postgres 2g/2cpu, pgbouncer 256m/0.5cpu, redis 512m/1cpu — all overridable from .env.prod. The comment says the defaults suit a ~4 GB host.

The API's own connection ceiling is TENANT_CLIENT_CACHE_SIZE (50) x TENANT_DB_POOL_MAX (5) = 250 against max_connections=200, and `pinWorkerConnLimit()` (the documented mitigation in four cron jobs) is a no-op under Prisma 7 driver adapters.

scripts/fleet-report.ts is the capacity/census tool the handbook never mentions: tenant census by status/plan/cell, per-tenant DB + storage sizes, PG connections vs max, cache hit ratio, Redis memory, storage-volume disk. Read-only, supports --json.

EMAIL_DRIVER=console in production withholds the body: `isDev` is false under NODE_ENV=production so the driver logs only a warn line with providerId/subject/recipient and explicitly states '(body withheld)'. No reset link ever reaches docker logs.

A Redis outage 500s every request including /healthz, /readyz, /metrics and the /admin/system-mode recovery lever: the ALWAYS_PASS branch still awaits `this.modes.resolveGlobal()`, and readCache/writeCache call `this.redis.client.get/set` with no catch.

Pulling the maintenance lever crashes signed-in tenant users rather than showing the takeover screen (frontend-03, high): the tenant layout awaits Promise.all([currentSystemMode, currentImpersonation]) before the takeover branch, and currentImpersonation rethrows non-401/403.

An unauthenticated caller can lock every platform admin out of the control plane: the admin lockout is keyed on the account alone (no IP component) and AdminAuthGuard rejects on status !== 'active', so it also kills existing valid admin sessions. Only a successful login clears it.

Session cookies are logged verbatim: the pino redact list covers only req.headers.authorization and req.headers.cookie, so response `set-cookie` is written into INFO logs on every login, signup, admin login, impersonation redemption and sliding-session refresh.

The scheduled-job health surface actively lies: the runner stores only {at, message, ok:true} and discards result.counts, so a sweep in which every tenant failed still reports ok:true. The libriant_worker_jobs_total metric referenced in jobs.types.ts does not exist.

facts.fact: The monitoring stack is exactly four services and contains NO Alertmanager: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0, prom/node-exporter:v1.8.2, gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor:v0.49.1, grafana/grafana-oss:11.4.0.
The Alertmanager wiring in Prometheus is commented out. The only live directive is `rule_files: - /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml`; the `alerting:`/`alertmanagers:` stanza is inside a comment block.

alerts.yml defines exactly 10 rules: TargetDown, LibriantApiDown, HostLowMemory, HostSwapping, HostDiskFilling, HostDiskCritical, HostHighCPU, LibriantPgConnectionsHigh, LibriantPgConnectionsCritical, LibriantPgCacheHitLow. Every one is a liveness, host-capacity or Postgres-capacity rule. None can express an error rate or a latency.
alerts.yml's own header states the rules are only 'visible in the Prometheus + Grafana Alerts views' until an Alertmanager is wired.

Nothing in the repo deploys or starts the monitoring stack. `grep -rn monitoring scripts/ .github/workflows/` returns zero matches. It is a manual `docker compose -f infra/monitoring/docker-compose.monitoring.yml up -d` only.

Grafana provisioning consists of ONE file — a Prometheus datasource. No dashboards are provisioned and no alerting/contact-point provisioning directory exists. A fresh Grafana boots with a working datasource and an empty dashboard list.
Grafana is published on 127.0.0.1:3300 (container port 3000). It is not reachable off-box without an SSH tunnel.

No service in the monitoring compose file declares mem_limit, cpus or pids_limit, whereas every service in the production compose file does (caddy 256m, api 1g, web 768m, worker 1g, postgres 2g, pgbouncer 256m, redis 512m). Adding monitoring to the box adds unbounded memory demand next to a capped app stack.

Prometheus scrape targets are exactly five jobs: prometheus (localhost:9090), node (node-exporter:9100), cadvisor (cadvisor:8080), libriant-api (api:3001/metrics), libriant-worker (worker:3002/metrics). There is no job for caddy, web, postgres or redis.

The commented-out postgres-exporter and redis-exporter declare `networks: [monitoring, app]`, but postgres and redis are ONLY on the `data` network, which is declared `internal: true`. As written, uncommenting them cannot work — the hostnames `postgres` and `redis` do not resolve from `app`. The exporters would need to join the project's `data` network instead.

Prometheus scraping api:3001 and worker:3002 DOES work: api is on `networks: [app, data]` and worker on `networks: [app, data]`, and the monitoring compose attaches Prometheus to the external `app` network, defaulting to `libriant_app`, which matches COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=libriant.

Caddy runs with `admin off`, so Caddy's own Prometheus endpoint (normally on the admin API at :2019/metrics) does not exist, and no `metrics` directive is configured in any site block. The edge — the only publicly exposed component — exports zero metrics.
facts.source: infra/caddy/Caddyfile:34; grep -n metrics infra/caddy/Caddyfile (only path matchers)

facts.fact: The API's /metrics exposes exactly eight gauges: libriant_api_uptime_seconds, libriant_api_build_info, libriant_tenants_total{status}, libriant_storage_used_bytes, libriant_pg_connections, libriant_pg_connections_max, libriant_pg_cache_hit_ratio, libriant_redis_used_memory_bytes. There is no request counter, no status-code breakdown and no latency histogram.

The capacity gauges are TTL-cached for 15 s and each source is isolated with Promise.allSettled — a failing source omits its gauge rather than breaking the scrape. So a missing gauge in Prometheus means that subsystem failed, not that the API is down.

The worker's /metrics exposes only libriant_worker_uptime_seconds and libriant_worker_jobs_running{queue} for the five queues (email-outbox, scheduled, import, maintenance, export). There is no per-job success/failure gauge.

The API's /metrics returns 404 to any request carrying x-real-ip, x-forwarded-for or x-forwarded-host — defence-in-depth so a proxy regression cannot expose fleet-wide tenant counts. Prometheus must therefore scrape api:3001 directly on the private network, never through Caddy.

There is no error tracker or APM anywhere in the codebase: grep for sentry/opentelemetry/otel/datadog/newrelic/bugsnag across apps/ packages/ package.json returns nothing. The only durable record of an exception is the container's stdout.
Container logs use the json-file driver at max-size 50m x max-file 5 per service — a ~250 MB ceiling per container, ~1.75 GB across the seven app services, all on the Docker data root.

Caddy writes a JSON access log to /var/log/caddy/access.log with roll_size 100mb and roll_keep 14 — up to ~1.4 GB. That volume (caddy_logs) is NOT rebound by the volume overlay, so unlike pg_data/redis_data/storage/caddy_data it stays on the Docker data root, not on $LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT.

It is NOT gated on MAINTENANCE_HARD, and it is imported into all three HTTPS vhosts (app host, admin host, marketing site). facts.fact: The plaintext :80 probe block does the same — `@probe path /healthz /readyz` -> `respond "ok" 200`. The caddy container healthcheck is `wget -qO- http://localhost:80/healthz`, so it is a self-test that cannot go red while the Caddy process is alive.

Web /api/healthz is a constant and its own comment says it 'Doesn't touch the API or any other dependency'. pgbouncer's healthcheck is `pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 -U libriant`, which the pooler answers itself without reaching Postgres, and api declares `pgbouncer: condition: service_started` — so the pooler's health status is read by nothing and cannot go red for the failure that matters.

The deploy's post-deploy health gate waits up to 180 s for five signals: `edge` (Caddy's static ok — proves nothing about the app), `site` (marketing vhost over --resolve to 127.0.0.1), and docker health for api, web and worker. api=healthy and worker=healthy are real deep probes; web=healthy is the constant. On failure the deploy gate explicitly does NOT roll back: 'Deploy finished but the stack is not healthy. Nothing was rolled back — inspect and re-run.'

`restart: unless-stopped` is the policy for every long-running service, and Docker Compose does not restart a container merely because its healthcheck is failing. An api container stuck 'unhealthy' stays up serving 500s indefinitely, unreported.

WHAT REACHES A HUMAN TODAY: nothing. No Alertmanager, no Grafana contact point, no external uptime monitor, no on-call destination, no error tracker. Detection time for any outage is 'until the operator next looks', which the handbook itself sets at weekly.

FAILURE MODE — Redis memory: mem_limit is 512m with NO `--maxmemory`, which makes the configured `--maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru` inert (the compose file reads as if a protection exists when none does). There is no soft landing between fine and cgroup-OOM-killed, and a killed Redis is a 100% outage per the Redis-down mode. Measured usage at 50 seeded tenants was 1.4 MB, so this is a long-horizon risk, not a launch one. The gauge libriant_redis_used_memory_bytes already exists and has no alert rule.

FAILURE MODE — connection exhaustion: TENANT_CLIENT_CACHE_SIZE (50) x TENANT_DB_POOL_MAX (5) = 250 possible tenant connections against max_connections=200, and pgbouncer fronts only libriant_control (DB_NAME: libriant_control) while tenant URLs derive from PG_SUPERUSER_URL pointing at postgres:5432 directly. The LibriantPgConnectionsHigh/Critical rules are the right signal for this and are the only rules that would catch it.

FAILURE MODE — deploy 502s: no reverse_proxy block sets lb_try_duration or lb_try_interval, and three blocks (the webhook proxy at :189 and both web:3000 blocks at :194 and :235) set no passive health at all. With a single upstream Caddy makes one attempt and returns 502 on connection refusal; on the api path `fail_duration 10s` can amplify a 200 ms restart into a 10-second blackout. Every manual `docker compose up -d` is therefore a user-visible 502 window.

Scheduled BullMQ jobs are upserted with no `attempts` and no `backoff`, so BullMQ's default attempts:1 applies and they never retry — despite the code comment at runner line 110 saying 're-throw so BullMQ marks the job failed + retries'. Recovery is only the next tick, so an hourly job loses a full hour to a 2-second blip.

Abandoned ('dead') email-outbox rows have no operator surface at all — no admin route, no metric, no /healthz field, no sweep. The rows are durable and carry lastError/failedAt/abandonedAt, so recovery is by SQL only. Dormant while EMAIL_DRIVER=console; live the moment a real provider is configured.

The pull-based operational surfaces that DO work: the admin Capacity page (sidebar label 'Capacity', route /admin/fleet) backed by GET /admin/fleet/overview (tenant census, per-tenant DB + storage sizes, PG connections vs max, cache hit ratio, Redis memory, storage disk), and the CLI `pnpm fleet:report`. Both are pull-only — nobody is notified.

The product ships incident levers the incident runbook never mentions: MAINTENANCE_HARD (a Caddy env var that serves a static maintenance page for every browser request while keeping probes at 200), the SystemModeKind states (normal/maintenance/read_only/out_of_order/under_construction) with an admin page, and an announcements feature that pushes a banner to tenants.

The DR path is now sound for Postgres and is exercised in CI: scripts/dr-drill.sh runs via `pnpm dr:drill` against a dedicated postgres service, plus a `--cross-cluster` variant, and scripts/_lib/pg-restore-filter.sh exists. What the drill does NOT cover: the storage tarball, backup.sh itself, restore.sh itself, and the rclone off-site round trip.

An aborted dr-drill.sh leaves the shared role with `statement_timeout=1s` and `CONNECTION LIMIT 7` because the EXIT trap only restores the password, not the deliberate drift. Symptom on the next stack that uses that role: 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' and 'too many connections for role', pointing nowhere near a shell script that exited earlier.

Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode / high security level serves a managed challenge that 403s curl and uptime probes. Reaching an external monitor to any origin path requires a WAF custom rule (Security -> WAF -> Custom rules) skipping the probe path. The deploy deliberately does not depend on the public URL for this reason.

Today nothing external is checkable at all: ports 80 and 443 are closed on 195.201.13.95, libriant.com resolves to Cloudflare with no origin (the audit measured `curl --max-time 15 https://libriant.com/` -> 000), and app.libriant.com has no DNS record. Any 'uptime monitor' step in the runbook is a post-cutover step, not a pre-cutover one.

Each one imports `cloudflare_origin`. A DNS plan that omits any of these four names leaves a configured vhost unreachable.

The `cloudflare_origin` snippet is a single static-file TLS directive: `tls /etc/caddy/origin/origin.crt /etc/caddy/origin/origin.key` (Caddyfile:120). An explicit `tls <cert> <key>` disables Caddy's automatic certificate management for that site — no ACME is attempted for ANY vhost. The reason, stated in the snippet's own comment: Cloudflare terminates public TLS, so an HTTP-01/TLS-ALPN-01 challenge never reaches the origin.

A second, independent reason ACME cannot work on 195.201.13.95 as it stands: ports 80 and 443 are closed externally (task briefing), and both HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01 require inbound 80/443 from the public internet. Even un-proxying a record would not rescue ACME while the firewall is Cloudflare-only, which is the very lockdown the runbook prescribes.

BREAK MODE C — an origin cert that exists but is expired or has the wrong SANs. deploy-on-host.sh:64 checks only that the two FILES exist; it never parses them. env.ts uses five resolution helpers with distinct failure semantics: required() throws on unset OR whitespace-only; requiredSecret(key, devFallback, nodeEnv, minLen=24) uses the dev fallback only when nodeEnv==='development', otherwise requires the key and additionally throws if length < minLen (the length bar is skipped when nodeEnv==='test'); optional(key, fallback) treats empty string as absent; num() returns the fallback for unset/blank but throws on non-finite, non-integer (when int:true) or out-of-range; bool() returns the fallback for unset/blank.

bool() accepts ONLY 'true','1','yes','on' (lower-cased, trimmed) as true. Any other string — 'enabled', 'y', 'TRUE '+junk — silently resolves to false with no warning. This is how BILLING_ENABLED and ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED are parsed.

NODE_ENV is a bare cast with no allow-list: `(process.env.NODE_ENV ?? 'development') as AppEnv['nodeEnv']`. Four protections key on the string being exactly 'production'. It is NOT operator-supplied in this deployment: it is a literal in compose (x-app-env and the web block) and an ENV in the API image, so .env.prod cannot override it.

facts.fact: RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED is also in that never-injected set, which is a safety property: even a stray RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=true in .env.prod cannot reach a container. Two independent in-code guards exist anyway — main.ts refuses to boot in production, and RateLimitService logs an error and ignores it.

Six keys are hard-required at the COMPOSE layer with `${VAR:?...}` — a missing one aborts `docker compose up` before any container is created, with a named error: POSTGRES_PASSWORD, HASH_PEPPER, SESSION_SECRET, ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, MFA_MASTER_KEY.

SESSION_SECRET — required in prod, min 24 chars, no default outside dev (dev fallback 'dev-only-session-secret-CHANGE-IN-PROD'). Generated by ensure-env.sh as `openssl rand -hex 32`. Read by CookieService and every session JWT path. Missing ⇒ compose aborts; empty-but-present ⇒ 'Missing required env var: SESSION_SECRET'; too short ⇒ 'Env var SESSION_SECRET is too short'. Rotating it logs out every library user.

ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET — same contract as SESSION_SECRET, deliberately distinct so a leaked tenant cookie cannot become an admin cookie. Dev fallback 'dev-only-admin-session-secret-CHANGE-IN-PROD'. Rotating logs out all platform admins.
IMPERSONATION_SECRET — same contract; signs support/impersonation session JWTs, distinct from the admin secret. Dev fallback 'dev-only-impersonation-secret-CHANGE-IN-PROD'.

MFA_MASTER_KEY — required in prod AND validated at boot against /^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/ (32 bytes for AES-256-GCM). A short/typo'd key exits the process with 'Env var MFA_MASTER_KEY must be 64 hex characters (a 32-byte key).' Dev fallback is the committed literal '0011223344...0011'. It is the ONLY thing that can decrypt stored admin TOTP secrets; secrets.ts classifies rotation as 'never'.

HASH_PEPPER — requiredSecret with minLen 32 (not 24), deliberately no production fallback because it peppers the IP hash behind the marketing application form's throttle and the privacy notice promises a secret key. Dev fallback 'libriant-dev-only'. Read only by ApplicationsService.

STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET — in production only, resolved via requiredSecret so it must be explicitly set (min 24); in dev/test it silently falls back to sessionSecret. Compose passes `${STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET:-}`, so an unset value arrives as an empty string and required() throws 'Missing required env var: STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET'. Read by SignedUrlService. Rotating 403s outstanding signed download links until reissued.

POSTGRES_PASSWORD — generated as `openssl rand -hex 24`; validated by secrets.ts to be URL-safe because it is interpolated into postgresql:// URLs (CONTROL_DATABASE_URL, PG_SUPERUSER_URL, pgbouncer DB_PASSWORD). Postgres applies it only at initdb; once the cluster exists the value in .env.prod must match pg_authid or every connection fails auth. Classified rotation:'never'.

The POSTGRES_PASSWORD 'CRITICAL guard' in ensure-env.sh does not work in the scenario it was written for. pg_data_initialized() asks `docker volume inspect` for a mountpoint and looks for PG_VERSION there, but the deploy always chains docker-compose.volume.yml which rebinds pg_data to ${LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT}/postgres — a local-driver bind volume still reports .Mountpoint as /var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data, which holds no PG_VERSION. On a boot-disk rebuild /var/lib/docker is gone entirely and docker may not even be installed, so the function returns 1 and the guard never fires. Result: a fresh password is minted over a surviving cluster and .env.prod is overwritten in the act of failing.

STRIPE_DRIVER — env.ts defaults to 'fake' in development and 'real' in every other environment; only the literals 'real'/'fake' are honoured, anything else falls to the environment default. ensure-env.sh writes STRIPE_DRIVER=fake on every deploy and compose defaults `${STRIPE_DRIVER:-fake}`, so production runs the fake driver unless an operator edits it.

PRODUCTION LANDMINE — STRIPE_DRIVER=fake is an unauthenticated remote-write vulnerability, not merely a no-charge stand-in. FakeStripeDriver hardcodes `private secret = 'fake-webhook-secret-for-dev'` and setSecret() has no non-test caller, so POST /webhooks/stripe (unauthenticated by design, and exempted from maintenance mode) accepts any event signed with that repo-published literal. The auditor executed this end-to-end and moved a real tenant from starter→institutional with HTTP 200 and no credential.

STRIPE_DRIVER=real fails loudly and safely: RealStripeDriver's constructor throws 'STRIPE_API_KEY is required when STRIPE_DRIVER=real' and then 'STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is required when STRIPE_DRIVER=real'. So the safe posture for a box that is not taking payments is NOT `fake` — it is `real` with keys, or the product's billing routes disabled.
STRIPE_API_KEY / STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET — read as `process.env.X?.length ? X : null`, so empty string becomes null. Both are external (pasted from Stripe) and are only consulted by the real driver.

BILLING_ENABLED — bool, default false. It is NOT the authoritative switch: PlatformSettingsService reads a platform_settings DB row and only falls back to env.billingEnabled when the row is absent, and the owner-only admin 'Subscriptions' toggle writes that row. Nothing cross-validates enforcement-on against STRIPE_DRIVER=fake, on either the env path or the admin-toggle path.

EMAIL_DRIVER — env.ts defaults to 'console' in development and 'smtp' in every other environment; only 'console'|'smtp'|'resend' are honoured. Compose deliberately passes it through UNSET (`${EMAIL_DRIVER:-}`) with a REL-06 comment explaining that a `:-console` default was removed so a forgetful operator gets a loud boot failure instead of silent non-delivery.

PRODUCTION LANDMINE — ensure-env.sh:101 writes `EMAIL_DRIVER=console` into .env.prod, and it runs with --auto on EVERY deploy before compose reads the file, so the compose fail-fast is unreachable and an operator who deletes the line gets it re-added on the next deploy. Two files in the same deploy path assert opposite policies.

With EMAIL_DRIVER=console in a non-dev environment, nothing is delivered AND the body is deliberately withheld from logs: ConsoleEmailDriver logs only a warn line with provider id / subject / recipient. The outbox row still gets a fabricated `console-<hex>` providerId, so the admin view reads as delivered. Password reset, email verification, support-key delivery and staff invites are therefore dead ends with no operator-side recovery path.

EMAIL_DRIVER=smtp requires SMTP_URL or SmtpEmailDriver throws at construction: 'EMAIL_DRIVER=smtp requires SMTP_URL (e.g. smtp://user:pass@host:587).' The transport is verified in the BACKGROUND, so a wrong host does not block boot — it logs 'SMTP verify failed: … — sends will retry.'

EMAIL_DRIVER=resend requires RESEND_API_KEY or ResendEmailDriver throws 'EMAIL_DRIVER=resend requires RESEND_API_KEY (re_...).' RESEND_API_KEY is listed in x-app-env only because of audit finding A5-01 — an unlisted key would be dropped by compose and crash-loop api+worker.

EMAIL_FROM defaults to `Libriant <no-reply@${PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN}>` — note it derives from the APEX, not from PUBLIC_HOST, contradicting .env.prod.example:85 which says it defaults to no-reply@${PUBLIC_HOST}. Compose passes `${EMAIL_FROM:-}` so an unset value in .env.prod reaches the container as empty and the env.ts default applies.
EMAIL_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5) is read by EmailService but is one of the 19 never-injected variables, so the retry budget is fixed at 5 in production.

PUBLIC_HOST is the APP host (app.libriant.com). It is not read by env.ts at all — compose derives PUBLIC_APP_URL, BILLING_RETURN_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL from it, and the caddy service + Caddyfile use it as a vhost name. Its default disagrees inside one file: x-app-env and the web block default to `libriant.com`, the caddy block and Caddyfile:149 default to `app.libriant.com`.

PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN (default 'localhost' in code, 'libriant.com' from ensure-env.sh) drives (a) tenant-subdomain resolution in TenantMiddleware, (b) the CSRF Origin allow-list in OriginCheckMiddleware, and (c) the defaults for ADMIN_HOST, SITE_HOST, EMAIL_FROM and APPLY_NOTIFY_TO. It does NOT drive cookie scope.
Session/admin/impersonation cookies carry no `domain` attribute and use the `__Host-` name prefix whenever secure, which forbids Domain — they are host-only by construction.

SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE defaults to 'auto', which resolves to secure in every environment other than development/test (or when PUBLIC_APP_URL is https). Compose overrides it with the literal 'true', so cookies are always Secure + __Host- prefixed in production regardless of .env.prod.

ADMIN_HOST (default `admin.${PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN}`) is load-bearing three times: it is excluded from tenant-subdomain resolution, it is the only Origin allowed for state-changing /admin/* requests, and the web app 404s /admin routes on any other host. It is passed to api/worker/migrate, to caddy, and separately to web.
SITE_HOST (default = PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN) is the marketing-site vhost. The Caddyfile deliberately gives it no /lbr-api/* handler, so any browser call that resolves the API base to SITE_HOST 404s.

APPLY_NOTIFY_TO (default `info@${PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN}`) is where new marketing-form applications are notified. It is interpolated by compose but is absent from .env.prod.example and from ensure-env.sh, so no operator will ever see it.

facts.fact: ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED defaults to !isDev — i.e. ON in production — and is one of the never-injected variables, so it cannot be turned off from .env.prod. Combined with no recovery-code field on AdminUser, a single admin, and MFA_MASTER_KEY being the only decryptor of the stored TOTP secret, losing the phone locks the operator out of the admin panel.

ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL / ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD are injected only into the one-shot `migrate` service, and prod-bootstrap.sh runs `pnpm admin:bootstrap` only when BOTH are non-empty; otherwise it prints 'ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_* not set - skipping admin creation' and the deploy still goes green. ensure-env.sh --auto never fills them, so a CI/manual deploy without a prior interactive run produces a stack nobody can log into. deploy-on-host.sh warns about the empty email but does not fail.

bootstrap-admin.ts is NOT create-only: when the email already exists it UPDATES passwordHash and role and resets failedAttempts=0, lockedUntil=null, status='active', disabledAt=null. Since prod-bootstrap.sh runs it on every deploy, leaving ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD in .env.prod re-applies that password and re-enables a disabled admin at every deploy. There is no admin password-change endpoint anywhere in apps/api, so this is in fact the only admin password-reset mechanism.

CONTROL_DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, PG_SUPERUSER_URL and STORAGE_ROOT are optional() with production-shaped localhost fallbacks (including the guessable libriant:libriant superuser). All four are compose literals so no deployment can reach the fallbacks, but anything run outside compose (a host-level `pnpm start`, a one-off script) silently gets them. Executed evidence: unset PG_SUPERUSER_URL and unset STORAGE_ROOT both boot fully green with readyz=200.

CONTROL_DATABASE_URL points at pgbouncer:5432 (transaction pooling) while PG_SUPERUSER_URL points at postgres:5432 directly. prod-bootstrap.sh deliberately re-exports CONTROL_DATABASE_URL=PG_SUPERUSER_URL for the migration/seed step because Prisma Migrate's session-level advisory lock is silently broken by a transaction-mode pooler.

ASSETS_ROOT and LOCALES_ROOT are set on api/worker/migrate — which read NEITHER (env.assetsRoot has no consumer anywhere in apps/api; LOCALES_ROOT appears nowhere in apps/api, and scripts/ingest-help-articles.ts computes its own path from __dirname) — and are NOT set on the web service, which is the only thing that reads them. The web container's read-only mounts of ../../assets and ../../locales are therefore inert: editing them on the host changes nothing.

facts.fact: ACME_EMAIL is effectively dead. The Caddyfile sets `email {$ACME_EMAIL:ops@libriant.com}` globally, but every HTTPS vhost imports the `cloudflare_origin` snippet which serves a file certificate from /etc/caddy/origin/, so no ACME order is ever placed. MAINTENANCE_HARD (default false) reaches only the caddy container and is the edge-level maintenance override; the normal lever is system-mode in the DB.

IMAGE_OWNER + IMAGE_TAG name the GHCR images. On the manual path this matters less than the docs imply: deploy-on-host.sh BUILDS locally (`dc build`) rather than pulling, and exports IMAGE_TAG=<12-char SHA>[-dirty] AFTER sourcing .env.prod precisely so the file's `IMAGE_TAG=latest` cannot clobber it. The CI path pulls instead.

COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=libriant and LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT=/mnt/libriant are written into .env.prod by ensure-env.sh but are also force-exported by both deploy paths after sourcing, so the file values are advisory. LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT is what the volume overlay binds pg_data/redis_data/storage/caddy_data to, and what backup.sh's docker-volume lookups key on via COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME.

Eight resource-limit knobs are interpolated by compose but documented nowhere: CADDY_MEM_LIMIT/CADDY_CPUS (256m/1), API_MEM_LIMIT/API_CPUS (1g/1.5), WEB_MEM_LIMIT/WEB_CPUS (768m/1), WORKER_MEM_LIMIT/WORKER_CPUS (1g/1), PG_MEM_LIMIT/PG_CPUS (2g/2), PGBOUNCER_MEM_LIMIT/PGBOUNCER_CPUS (256m/0.5), REDIS_MEM_LIMIT/REDIS_CPUS (512m/1). The defaults sum to ~5.8 GB and suit a ~4 GB host per the file's own comment; the new box's RAM is unknown.

Backup/restore env is a separate, undocumented namespace read only by the shell scripts, never by compose: BACKUP_ROOT (default /srv/libriant/backups — the BOOT DISK), BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS (14), RCLONE_REMOTE (empty), BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL, BACKUP_ALLOW_LOCAL_ONLY, BACKUP_ALLOW_NO_STORAGE, BACKUP_ALLOW_OFFHOST_TENANTS, STORAGE_DIR, CADDY_LOG_DIR, COMPOSE_FILE, LIBRIANT_APP_DIR. Of these only BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS and RCLONE_REMOTE exist in .env.prod.example, and BACKUP_ROOT is not settable there at all — it must be set inline in the cron line.

backup.sh does not capture .env.prod — the archive is pg_dumpall + a tar of the storage volume + the last day of Caddy access log. This is deliberate (a stolen backup would otherwise be total compromise) and is what makes the secrets irrecoverable from backups. Note that pg_dumpall globals carry only the SCRAM verifier for the libriant role, not the plaintext POSTGRES_PASSWORD.

IRRECOVERABLE IF LOST (nothing on disk or in any backup can regenerate them): MFA_MASTER_KEY (the only decryptor of stored admin TOTP secrets — losing it orphans every enrolment and, with MFA mandatory in prod, locks the admin panel), POSTGRES_PASSWORD (the running cluster is keyed to it; a mismatch fails every connection and ensure-env.sh's guard will not catch it), and the Cloudflare Origin Certificate pair origin.crt/origin.key (deploy-on-host.sh states 'It is in the password manager — no backup contains it'; a missing pair fails the deploy at the `caddy validate` step with a misleading 'Caddyfile is invalid').

RECOVERABLE BUT DISRUPTIVE IF LOST (regenerable, at a cost): SESSION_SECRET (logs out every library user), ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET (logs out all admins), IMPERSONATION_SECRET (kills live support sessions), STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET (403s outstanding signed download links), HASH_PEPPER (resets the application-form IP throttle history).

Only three secrets live outside .env.prod: GITHUB_TOKEN (auto-provisioned by Actions), DEPLOY_SSH_KEY and DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS, all GitHub Actions repository secrets. fleet.yml records that DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS still pins the DEAD host's SSH keys and must be re-keyed before any workflow_dispatch run against 195.201.13.95.

ensure-env.sh's contract: umask 077, mkdir -p, touch, chmod 600 on the env file; ensure_rand/ensure_default NEVER overwrite a non-empty value; free-text values go through set_quoted which refuses any value containing a single quote. It generates 6 hex-32 secrets plus POSTGRES_PASSWORD hex-24, writes 12 config defaults, prompts for 3 operator values only when --auto is absent, and finally syncs any key present in .env.prod.example but absent from the file, copying the template line verbatim (skipping IMAGE_OWNER).

The template-sync step is why STRIPE_API_KEY=, SMTP_URL=, RESEND_API_KEY=, EMAIL_FROM=, EMAIL_REPLY_TO=, MAINTENANCE_HARD=false, RCLONE_REMOTE=, BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS=14 and DESKTOP_RELEASE_REPO=CyberSystema/libriant appear in .env.prod even though the explicit logic never writes them.

It is INCOMPLETE: HASH_PEPPER, RESEND_API_KEY and DESKTOP_RELEASE_TOKEN are absent, so `pnpm secrets audit` cannot report them missing — and HASH_PEPPER is one of the six keys compose hard-requires.
