facts.fact: OVERARCHING: no host has ever run this stack. The three-host layout (a3ad916), Node 26 (a04cf82), Redis 8 + pgbouncer 1.25.2 (84e61ff) and the baked-site Caddy image all landed 2026-08-22 — the same day the old box died. Neither .github/workflows/ci.yml nor verify.yml contains any `docker build`, `docker compose` or `caddy validate` step (grep returns nothing). The only place the images are built and the only place the Caddyfile is validated is on the box itself (scripts/deploy-on-host.sh:130,138). The first `bash scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` on 195.201.13.95 will be the first time this topology has ever been assembled anywhere.
facts.source: git log --format='%h %ad %s' -- infra/; grep -rn 'docker compose|docker build|caddy validate' .github/workflows/{ci,verify}.yml (no output); scripts/deploy-on-host.sh:130,138

facts.fact: The prod stack is EIGHT compose services, not seven: caddy, migrate, api, web, worker, postgres, pgbouncer, redis. Seven are long-running; `migrate` is a one-shot that must exit 0 before api and worker are allowed to start.

THREE images are built, not two: ghcr.io/${IMAGE_OWNER:-libriant}/libriant-caddy (infra/caddy/Dockerfile), -api (apps/api/Dockerfile), -web (apps/web/Dockerfile). The api image is used by THREE services — api, worker and migrate — so an api-image defect takes down migrations, the API and every background job at once.

Image tags: deploy-on-host.sh sets IMAGE_TAG to the 12-char short SHA plus `-dirty` if the tree is dirty, and exports it AFTER sourcing .env.prod (which ships IMAGE_TAG=latest) so the env file cannot clobber it. It BUILDS locally and never pulls — nothing publishes to GHCR while deploys are manual.

Only caddy publishes host ports: 80:80/tcp, 443:443/tcp, 443:443/udp (HTTP/3). No other service has a `ports:` key. Docker publishes on 0.0.0.0 and inserts DOCKER-USER rules that bypass ufw's INPUT chain.

Three networks. `edge` (bridge) — caddy only. `app` (bridge, has internet egress) — caddy, api, web, worker. `data` (bridge, internal: true, NO route to host or internet) — postgres, pgbouncer, redis, api, worker, migrate. web is on `app` ONLY and therefore cannot reach Postgres or Redis at all. migrate is on `data` ONLY and therefore has NO internet egress.

BLOCKER supply-chain-06, and it is a topology fact: package.json:6 declares `packageManager: pnpm@11.22.0` (bumped in fe0931e) but all three Dockerfiles run `corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate`. The api runtime stage is `FROM base` (not `deps`), so only 9.15.4 is in /opt/corepack; `USER node` (Dockerfile:97) runs prod-bootstrap.sh:35 → `pnpm db:migrate:deploy` from /app, corepack tries to fetch 11.22.0, and migrate is on the `data` network which is `internal: true` — no egress, no fallback. migrate exits 1, and api + worker are gated on `migrate: condition: service_completed_successfully`, so the whole stack never starts.

The web image is worse than the api image on the same defect: apps/web/Dockerfile:9 prepares pnpm 9.15.4, sets NO COREPACK_HOME, and its CMD is `pnpm --filter @libriant/web start` as PID 1 under tini — so the web container fetches pnpm from npmjs.org over the `app` network on EVERY start and executes it on the boot path.

depends_on graph, exactly: pgbouncer→postgres(healthy); migrate→postgres(healthy) ONLY; api→migrate(completed_successfully)+postgres(healthy)+pgbouncer(**started**, not healthy)+redis(healthy); worker→migrate(completed_successfully)+postgres(healthy)+redis(healthy) — worker does NOT wait for pgbouncer even though its CONTROL_DATABASE_URL points at pgbouncer:5432; web→api(healthy); caddy→web(started)+api(started), deliberately loosened from healthy so an app outage cannot take the marketing site down.

Restart policies: caddy, api, web, worker, postgres, pgbouncer, redis all `restart: unless-stopped` (via the *restart anchor). migrate is `restart: 'no'`. `unless-stopped` restarts on process EXIT only — Docker does not restart a container that merely fails its healthcheck, and there is no autoheal sidecar. An api marked `unhealthy` will sit there unhealthy and serving 5xx forever.

Healthchecks, verbatim: caddy `wget -qO- http://localhost:80/healthz` 30s/5s/5 (no start_period); api `wget -qO- http://localhost:3001/readyz` 15s/5s/8, start_period 30s; web `wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/healthz` 15s/5s/8, start_period 30s; worker `wget -qO- http://localhost:3002/readyz` 30s/5s/5, start_period 20s; postgres `pg_isready -U libriant -d libriant_control` 10s/5s/10; pgbouncer `pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 -U libriant` 30s/5s/5; redis `redis-cli ping` 10s/3s/10. migrate has no healthcheck.

api /readyz returns 503 (ServiceUnavailableException) if EITHER Redis ping OR `SELECT 1` on the control DB fails. So a Redis outage marks the api container unhealthy — and per boot-and-config-01 it also 500s /healthz and every other route, including the /admin/system-mode recovery lever.

worker /readyz requires all FIVE queue consumers running (email-outbox, scheduled, import, maintenance, export) AND a live Redis ping; otherwise 503. All five run in ONE process, so an OOM of the export job (performance-01) takes the email outbox and all nine cron sweeps with it.

Resource caps (env-overridable defaults). mem_limit: caddy 256m, api 1g, web 768m, worker 1g, postgres 2g, pgbouncer 256m, redis 512m → sum 5888 MiB = 5.75 GiB. cpus: 1 + 1.5 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 0.5 + 1 = 8.0. pids_limit: 256/1024/512/512/512/256/256. migrate has NO mem_limit, NO cpus and NO pids_limit.
Logging: every service including migrate uses json-file with max-size 50m / max-file 5 → up to 250 MiB per service, ~2 GiB total, all on the BOOT disk under /var/lib/docker/containers.

Six named volumes: pg_data, redis_data, caddy_data, caddy_config, caddy_logs, storage. docker-compose.volume.yml binds only FOUR to the data root — pg_data→$LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT/postgres, redis_data→/redis, storage→/storage, caddy_data→/caddy. caddy_config and caddy_logs are NOT overlaid and stay as Docker-managed volumes on the boot disk.

caddy_logs living on the boot disk is confirmed by the backup script, which reads it at /var/lib/docker/volumes/${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_caddy_logs/_data. The Caddy access log is capped by Caddy itself at roll_size 100mb × roll_keep 14 ≈ 1.4 GB of boot disk.

LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT defaults to /mnt/libriant (compose:152, volume.yml:28/33/38/43, ensure-env.sh:112, deploy-on-host.sh:25). Docker's local driver with `o: bind` does NOT create a missing device path, so an unmounted volume is a safe hard failure rather than a silently-fresh database on the boot disk. deploy-on-host.sh:55-57 pre-checks postgres/redis/storage/caddy exist and dies with the real cause.

Bind mounts, complete list. caddy: infra/caddy/Caddyfile→/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro, infra/caddy/maintenance.html→/srv/libriant/caddy/maintenance.html:ro, <repo>/assets→/srv/libriant/assets:ro, $LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT/caddy/origin→/etc/caddy/origin:ro. api: <repo>/assets→/srv/libriant/assets:ro, <repo>/locales→/srv/libriant/locales:ro. web: same two. worker: same two. migrate: <repo>/scripts→/app/scripts:ro and <repo>/locales→/app/locales:ro (DIFFERENT mount points from api/web). postgres: infra/compose/postgres-init.sql→/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/00-init.sql:ro. On the host <repo> is /srv/libriant/app.

Because migrate bind-mounts the host checkout's scripts/ and locales/ over the image's copies, the bootstrap that runs is the HOST CHECKOUT's code running against the IMAGE's node_modules. With `--skip-build` those two can be different commits. The two mount points exist because scripts/ingest-help-articles.ts:25-26 resolves locales relative to its own file (/app/scripts/../locales).

The Cloudflare origin certificate MUST live on the host at $LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT/caddy/origin/origin.crt and origin.key (default /mnt/libriant/caddy/origin/), mounted read-only at /etc/caddy/origin. It is referenced by the (cloudflare_origin) snippet, which ALL FOUR https vhosts import. It is not in any backup — deploy-on-host.sh:64-68 dies with that exact message. Note it sits INSIDE the caddy_data bind (/mnt/libriant/caddy → /data), so the same files also appear at /data/origin inside the container; do not 'clean' /data.

Caddy serves FOUR https vhosts plus one plaintext block. (1) {$PUBLIC_HOST:app.libriant.com} — the app. (2) {$ADMIN_HOST:admin.libriant.com} — the admin panel. (3) {$SITE_HOST:libriant.com} — the static marketing site from /srv/libriant/site. (4) www.{$SITE_HOST} — permanent redirect to the apex. (5) `http://` — a plaintext catch-all that answers /healthz and /readyz with 'ok' 200 and permanent-redirects everything else to https. A commented-out wildcard *.{$PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN} block at :343-359 is NOT active and would need a DNS-01 provider plugin.

App vhost routing: handle_path /lbr-api/* → strips the prefix, then inside a `route` a @internal matcher 404s /metrics, /metrics/*, /healthz, /readyz, and everything else reverse_proxies to api:3001 with `header_up X-Real-IP {http.request.header.CF-Connecting-IP}`, fail_duration 10s, max_fails 3. handle /webhooks/* → api:3001 (no prefix strip, no X-Real-IP header_up). handle {} catch-all → web:3000.

Admin vhost routing: same handle_path /lbr-api/* with the same @internal 404 guard and X-Real-IP stamp (but NO fail_duration/max_fails). Then a `route` block — deliberately `route`, not `handle`, because a bare `handle @bare` was previously bypassed by the catch-all — that redirects `/` to /admin/login 302 and reverse_proxies everything else to web:3000. There is no /webhooks handler on the admin host.
facts.source: infra/caddy/Caddyfile:212-237 (comment at :226-231 records the observed bypass)

facts.fact: Marketing-site vhost: `encode zstd gzip`, root /srv/libriant/site, pretty URLs via `try_files {path} {path}.html`, file_server, and handle_errors serving /en/404.html for /en/* and /404.html otherwise. It has NO /lbr-api/* block on purpose (Caddyfile:246-250 warns that adding one would re-expose fleet-wide tenant counts). Its ONLY dependency on the app is @apply (paths /apply and /en/apply) reverse-proxied to api:3001 — so during an api outage the marketing site serves fine but /apply 502s. It deliberately does NOT import maintenance_takeover.

Security headers are split across two snippets. (security_headers) — used by the app and admin vhosts — sets HSTS max-age=31536000 includeSubDomains preload, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy camera=()/microphone=()/geolocation=(), and strips Server. It carries NO CSP: the app's CSP comes from Next.js instead (apps/web/next.config.mjs:55-81, applied to /:path*). (site_headers) — used only by the marketing site — repeats those and adds a strict CSP with script-src 'none'. The www redirect vhost imports NEITHER header snippet.

/healthz, /readyz and /metrics handling is layered and the public answer is a decoy. The (maintenance_check) snippet — imported by the app, admin AND site vhosts — matches path /healthz /readyz /metrics and does `respond "ok" 200` at the edge. Caddy never touches api or web for those paths. So `curl https://app.libriant.com/healthz` returning 200 proves ONLY that Caddy is alive. Real metrics are reachable only from inside the `app` network at api:3001/metrics and worker:3002/metrics.

The api additionally refuses /metrics defence-in-depth: it throws 404 if the request carries x-real-ip, x-forwarded-for or x-forwarded-host, on the theory that only a direct in-network Prometheus scrape lacks those. Caddy stamps X-Real-IP on everything it proxies, so a topology regression that exposed /metrics would still 404.

Prometheus is optional and out-of-stack. infra/monitoring/docker-compose.monitoring.yml is a separate compose project that joins the EXTERNAL network ${LIBRIANT_APP_NETWORK:-libriant_app} to scrape api:3001 and worker:3002. Grafana binds 127.0.0.1:3300 only (SSH tunnel). It is not started by deploy-on-host.sh or the deploy workflow.

Compose gets NO env_file. `grep -rn 'env_file|--env-file' infra/compose .github/workflows/deploy.yml scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` finds only the header comment. deploy-on-host.sh:98 does `set -a; . /srv/libriant/.env.prod; set +a` — shell environment, not Compose's env-file mechanism. .env.prod is at /srv/libriant/.env.prod, NOT adjacent to the compose file, so Compose's automatic `.env` discovery never fires either. Running `docker compose ... up` without sourcing that file fails immediately on `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?...}`.

THE #1 OPERATING RULE for env: Compose injects ONLY the variables literally referenced in the x-app-env block. A key added to .env.prod that is not in that block never reaches the container. The compose file says this twice, in scar-tissue comments (:59-60 for drivers, :79-82 for RESEND_API_KEY).

x-app-env is 33 keys, injected into api, worker and migrate: NODE_ENV, CONTROL_DATABASE_URL (→pgbouncer:5432/libriant_control), REDIS_URL (→redis:6379), PUBLIC_APP_URL, PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN, SITE_HOST, HASH_PEPPER, APPLY_NOTIFY_TO, ADMIN_HOST, TENANT_PATH_PREFIX=/t/, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=true, SESSION_SECRET, ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, MFA_MASTER_KEY, STORAGE_ROOT=/srv/libriant/storage, STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET, ASSETS_ROOT=/srv/libriant/assets, LOCALES_ROOT=/srv/libriant/locales, BILLING_ENABLED, STRIPE_DRIVER, STRIPE_API_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, BILLING_RETURN_URL, EMAIL_DRIVER, SMTP_URL, RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM, EMAIL_REPLY_TO, BCRYPT_COST=12, PG_SUPERUSER_URL (→postgres:5432, bypassing pgbouncer), DESKTOP_RELEASE_REPO, DESKTOP_RELEASE_TOKEN. Five of these fail the container at boot if unset: HASH_PEPPER, SESSION_SECRET, ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, IMPERSONATION_SECRET, MFA_MASTER_KEY (`${VAR:?...}`).

Many app tunables env.ts reads are NOT in x-app-env and therefore cannot be changed from .env.prod at all without editing the compose file: ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED, ADMIN_SESSION_TTL_SEC, BILLING_GRACE_PERIOD_DAYS, EMAIL_MAX_ATTEMPTS, LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MS, MAX_FAILED_LOGINS, SESSION_TTL_SEC, SESSION_REMEMBER_TTL_SEC, SESSION_ABSOLUTE_MAX_TTL_SEC, STORAGE_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, STORAGE_SIGNED_TTL_SEC, SUPPORT_KEY_TTL_SEC, SUPPORT_SESSION_TTL_SEC, TENANT_CACHE_TTL_SEC, TENANT_CLIENT_CACHE_SIZE, TENANT_CLIENT_IDLE_MS.

caddy receives only FIVE env vars: SITE_HOST, PUBLIC_HOST, ADMIN_HOST, ACME_EMAIL, MAINTENANCE_HARD. web receives only SEVEN: NODE_ENV=production, PORT=3000, NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, API_INTERNAL_URL=http://api:3001, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, PUBLIC_APP_URL, ADMIN_HOST. redis receives none.

The web container gets ASSETS_ROOT/LOCALES_ROOT set NOWHERE, so the /srv/libriant/assets and /srv/libriant/locales bind mounts on the web service are INERT — apps/web/lib/asset-root.ts:15 and apps/web/lib/locale-loader.ts:9 fall back to the copies baked into the image at build time. Only api and worker actually read the mounted copies (via x-app-env:54-55). 'Designers hot-swap assets' works for the API and for Caddy's /_assets/* file_server, not for Next.js.

In production the web container's Next rewrite for /lbr-api/:path* targets `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (the PUBLIC origin https://app.libriant.com), not API_INTERNAL_URL. So Caddy's handle_path /lbr-api/* is load-bearing: if it ever stopped matching, requests would fall to web:3000 and Next would rewrite them back out to the public origin — a loop through Cloudflare, not a clean failure. Caddy also serves /_assets/* itself from the bind mount, duplicating a Next rewrite to /api/assets/:path*.

Postgres: image postgres:16-alpine, POSTGRES_USER=libriant, POSTGRES_DB=libriant_control, LANG=el_GR.UTF-8, started with `-c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements -c max_connections=200`. postgres-init.sql creates unaccent, pg_trgm, pg_stat_statements, pgcrypto, citext plus a libriant_demo database. CRITICAL: /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d runs ONLY when PGDATA is empty — after a restore, or on any cluster that already exists, that file never executes.

pgbouncer: image edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0, POOL_MODE=transaction, AUTH_TYPE=scram-sha-256, MAX_CLIENT_CONN=500, DEFAULT_POOL_SIZE=20, listening on 5432 inside the container (dev maps it to host 6432). Migrations deliberately BYPASS it via PG_SUPERUSER_URL→postgres:5432 because Prisma Migrate's session-level advisory lock is broken by transaction pooling.

Redis: image redis:8-alpine, `redis-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`, with NO --maxmemory set on purpose — Redis also backs the BullMQ queues and an eviction policy could drop live job keys. Data in redis_data → /mnt/libriant/redis.

The Caddy edge image bakes the marketing site: infra/caddy/Dockerfile stage 1 is node:26-alpine, runs `pnpm --filter @libriant/site build` (strict, refuses to emit while site.config.json holds a [PLACEHOLDER]), and stage 2 is `FROM caddy:2-alpine` with dist copied to /srv/libriant/site. Consequences the runbook must state: changing marketing copy is a rebuild, not a file edit; a broken site build fails the deploy at `dc build`; and Caddy base-image CVE patches now require a rebuild rather than a `pull`.

Deploy sequence on the box, in order: precondition checks (git checkout, .env.prod, $DATA_ROOT and its four subdirs, docker, origin cert, ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL warning) → git fetch + `git reset --hard` (host-local edits to TRACKED files are DISCARDED) → compute IMAGE_TAG → ensure-env.sh --auto + source → `docker image prune -af --filter until=72h` and `docker builder prune -f` → `dc build` → `dc run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint caddy caddy validate` → `dc up -d --remove-orphans --force-recreate` (dumping migrate logs on failure) → `dc exec caddy caddy reload` with a force-recreate fallback → a 180s local health gate.

The health gate is deliberately local and checks five things every 5s for up to 180s: `curl http://localhost/healthz` == 200 (Caddy only), `curl -sk --resolve libriant.com:443:127.0.0.1 https://libriant.com/` == 200 (uses --resolve, not -H Host, because SNI must be libriant.com for the origin cert), and Docker health status == healthy for api, web and worker. It checks nothing through public DNS because the box is not in DNS. On timeout it does NOT roll back.

Caddy's config is a bind mount, so `up -d` will not restart it for a Caddyfile-only change — hence the explicit `caddy reload` step. The Caddyfile is validated with the origin cert present because Caddy provisions file certificates during `validate`; a missing cert makes validate report 'Caddyfile is invalid' when the Caddyfile is fine, which is why deploy-on-host.sh:59-68 pre-checks it.

BLOCKER authn-authz-01 is a Caddy-config fact: Caddyfile:177/219/276 unconditionally does `header_up X-Real-IP {http.request.header.CF-Connecting-IP}` with NO `remote_ip` matcher anywhere in the file's 359 lines, and the compose file publishes 80/443 to 0.0.0.0 bypassing ufw. Every rate limit, the /apply throttle and the login lockout key on that value. Any runbook step that says 'the firewall only admits Cloudflare' is describing something that does not exist.

BLOCKER billing-02 rides on the compose default: x-app-env:65 is `STRIPE_DRIVER: ${STRIPE_DRIVER:-fake}`, .env.prod.example:69 writes `fake`, and ensure-env.sh:100 writes `fake`. env.ts:352-359 would default an UNSET value to `real` in production, but nothing is unset — the toolchain sets it to fake at three layers. `POST /webhooks/stripe` is proxied straight to api:3001 by Caddy's handle /webhooks/* with no auth.

BLOCKER launch-readiness-01 likewise: compose passes EMAIL_DRIVER through unset-safe (`${EMAIL_DRIVER:-}`, deliberately NOT defaulting to console), but ensure-env.sh:101 writes `console` into .env.prod, so console it is. env.ts:376-384 would have defaulted an unset value to `smtp` and failed loudly. The chosen default converts a loud failure into a silent one.

Backups are host-side, not a compose service. scripts/backup.sh runs `dc exec -T postgres pg_dumpall`, tars the storage volume (resolved via `docker volume inspect ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_storage`), and tars the Caddy access log from the boot-disk volume path. BACKUP_ROOT defaults to /srv/libriant/backups (boot disk); COMPOSE_FILE defaults to the prod file WITHOUT the volume overlay, which is safe for `exec` because the named volumes are already mounted in the running containers.

MAINTENANCE_HARD is caddy-only and is the belt-and-braces edge fallback: when true, the (maintenance_takeover) handle is supposed to serve /srv/libriant/caddy/maintenance.html for every browser request on the app and admin vhosts, without touching upstream. The marketing-site vhost deliberately omits it. The in-DB system-mode middleware is the normal lever; this one is meant to survive a full app outage.
